subject: Post-demo recap — head-to-head burst & p95/p99 lab asks vs HyperscaleX
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Tremblay <alex@hyperscalex.com>, HyperscaleX Sales Eng <sales.eng@hyperscalex.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 May 2029 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap — head-to-head burst & p95/p99 lab asks vs HyperscaleX

Alex — thanks again for making time today. Quick recap from our side plus the lab asks so we can line up an apples-to-apples comparison next week. Short TL;DR and then the technical plan below.

TL;DR
- HyperscaleX is a good fit for low-concurrency, larger-batch offline workloads; they saw the demo but we should validate microburst and p95/p99 under steady-state concurrency.
- Redwood differentiators to validate on the lab: continuous batching with low tail-latency, prefix/KV cache hit behavior, and graceful fallback to a lower-cost quantized runtime under load.
- Ask: approve a 2-day head-to-head A/B probe (two configurations) with the test matrix below and share sample prompts + auth for HyperscaleX sandbox.

Requested A/B probe (proposed)
1) Objectives:
  - Measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec for short (avg 32 tokens), medium (avg 128), and long (avg 512) sequences.
  - Evaluate microburst behavior: 100 concurrent single-request spikes sustained for 30s every 5 minutes.
  - Compare throughput under batching vs no-batching to observe endpoint-level aggregation effects.
2) Workloads / test vectors:
  - We request the sample prompt set attached (sample-prompts-hx.csv). Please add any customer-specific prompts you want included.
3) Configs to run (each as separate runs):
  - Redwood baseline: production runtime, dynamic batching (max batch 128), KV cache enabled, FP16 quantized model variant.
  - Redwood conservative: pinned smaller batch (max 32), KV cache disabled (measure cold tails).
  - HyperscaleX baseline: your standard public API settings (please confirm exact model variant + any request-level timeouts).
4) Metrics to capture:
  - p50/p95/p99 latency (generation-only and total request).
  - tokens/sec observed at service-layer and client-layer.
  - error rates, 5xx spikes, and any queue/drop indications.
  - end-to-end cost-per-1M-tokens estimate (if you can provide).
5) Scheduling:
  - Prefer Wed/Thu next week (May 22–23) US-PST window midday. Let us know availability.

Next steps (from Redwood)
- Jonas will finalize the exact run scripts and share the Drive link to the runbook (attached PDF).
- Ben will stand up a quick Grafana dashboard for p95/p99 + tokens/sec so both teams can watch live.
- Alex: confirm HyperscaleX sandbox credentials + model variant and any rate-limiting we should be aware of.

Attachments: redwood-ab-probe-plan-v1.pdf (lab plan), sample-prompts-hx.csv

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0184

From: Alex Tremblay <alex@hyperscalex.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: HyperscaleX Sales Eng <sales.eng@hyperscalex.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 May 2029 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — head-to-head burst & p95/p99 lab asks vs HyperscaleX

Thanks Rachel — appreciate the clear plan. HyperscaleX can participate; a few clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

1) Model variant: we'll run against our public-inference v3.4 (FP16) and can expose a quantized-wa variant on request — would you like us to include that as a third arm?
2) Sandbox access: we'll create an API key scoped to your caller IPs and send credentials by EOD Monday.
3) Rate limiting: we have a soft per-key RPS limit that will be bumped for the test window; we'll share exact throttling config.

Microburst behavior: our team asks that you also capture connection-level metrics (open sockets and queue depth) since our surface-level batching happens inside the gateway — it helps correlate drops vs queueing.

We're tentatively good for Wed/Thu (May 22–23) 11:00–15:00 PST. Confirm and we'll provision the sandbox.

— Alex
Alex Tremblay
Principal SRE, HyperscaleX
alex@hyperscalex.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Tremblay <alex@hyperscalex.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — head-to-head burst & p95/p99 lab asks vs HyperscaleX

Alex — thanks, that makes sense. Quick notes on Redwood runbook and instrumentation we propose so results are comparable: 

- We'll publish a runbook link in the Drive that lists exact curl calls and the loader (wrk2-based) config; it will include client-side socket metrics and our server-side traces for queue depth.
- We'll include a third arm (Redwood quantized-wa) to match your quantized-wa if you spin one up — good call to include it for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- For microbursts: we will schedule three 30s spike windows (100 concurrent single-request clients) separated by 5 minutes. We'll also run a 30-minute steady-state run at 200 RPS to capture p99 under sustained load.

I've attached the initial run scripts to this thread (refer to redwood-ab-probe-plan-v1.pdf) — Ben and I will finalize by EOD and then Rachel can lock in the calendar.

Jonas Weber
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
